name: שָׁפָט
summary: Chiefly the father of Elisha, of Abel-meholah, on whose land Elijah found Elisha ploughing (1Ki 19:16, 19), so that the prophet is named as “Elisha son of Shaphat” (2Ki 3:11; 6:31). Also the spy sent from Simeon to search out Canaan; a descendant of David through Zerubbabel; a chief of Gad in Bashan; and the overseer of David’s herds in the valleys. The name is the verb itself, שָׁפָט “he has judged”, the perfect in its pausal form: a short form of names such as יְהוֹשָׁפָט and שְׁפַטְיָה that leaves the divine name unspoken, as Phoenician has špṭ beside špṭbʿl.

evidence.note: “Elisha son of שָׁפָט of Abel-meholah you shall anoint as prophet in your place.”
Elijah finds “Elisha son of שָׁפָט” ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle on him.
“Elisha son of שָׁפָט is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.”
The king swears against “the head of Elisha son of שָׁפָט”.
“For the tribe of Simeon, שָׁפָט son of Hori”, among the twelve spies.
Among the sons of Shemaiah, in the line of David after the exile: וְשָׁפָט.
“וְשָׁפָט in Bashan”, of the sons of Gad.
“Over the herds in the valleys was שָׁפָט son of Adlai.”
“There he judged (שָׁפָט) Israel”: the verb, of Samuel, in the very form of the name.

note: The name’s key (v.fg.ad) also counts 1Sa 7:17, the verb in pause, filed there by spelling; the verb’s key counts six of the name’s tokens. Phoenician–Punic špṭ (“Safot”), short for špṭ-DN or DN-špṭ, is the same short form (see phn-shptbl).
